title: Pointed-colimit comparison for an etale localization
statement: Let R be a commutative local ring with maximal ideal m, and let K be a separable closure of its residue field. Let c be a colimit cocone of the diagram of pointed etale R-algebra triples [lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples], with point C, structural map rho:R to C, and residue map psi:C to K satisfying rho=alpha_s followed by c_s and psi followed after c_s equal to the pointed residue map for every triple s. Fix a triple t=(S,q,phi), and let A=S_q, with its local-ring structure. Let chiA:kappa(A) to K be a residue embedding whose composite with S to A to kappa(A) equals S to kappa(q) to K. Let d be a colimit cocone of the pointed etale A-algebra triples for chiA, with point D, structural map delta:A to D, and residue map psiD:D to K satisfying the analogous cocone equations. There exists a unique ring equivalence e:D to C such that e composed with S to A to D equals the cocone map S to C, and psi composed with e equals psiD. No ideal or completion assertion is included.

source.place: Lemma Tag 06LJ (lemma-henselization-noetherian), proof part (c), paragraph beginning 'To finish the proof of (c)', using Algebra Tag 04GW (lemma-strict-henselization-different) and Tag 04GP (lemma-strict-henselization)

proof.text: Apply lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples to $(R,m,K)$ and to $(A,qA,K)$. The field $K$ is separably closed, and its given separable-algebraic extension structure over $\kappa(m)$ makes it separable algebraic over $\kappa(q)$ through the map induced by $S\to A$, so both constructions apply. They give strictly henselian local rings $C$ and $D=A^{\mathrm{sh}}$, with maximal ideals $m_C=mC$ and $m_D=qD$ and residue field $K$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 04GW and Lemma Tag 04GP, items (2)-(5)

proof.text: The composite $S\to C\to K$ equals $S\to\kappa(q)\to K$, so the preimage of $m_C$ in $S$ is $q$ by the preimage clause of lem-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-triples. Hence $S\to C$ sends every element outside $q$ to a unit and factors uniquely through the localization $A=S_q$. Thus the maps $S\to A\to C$ and $S\to C$ agree.

source.place: Lemma Tag 04GW, item (2), and the universal property of localization

proof.text: Use lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit over the base $A$ with source $D$, target $C$, and residue map the identity of $K$ to obtain the unique $A$-algebra map $f:D\to C$. Use the same lemma over the base $R$ with source $C$, target $D$, and residue map the identity of $K$ to obtain the unique $R$-algebra map $g:C\to D$. The hypotheses hold because each of $C$ and $D$ is a filtered colimit of etale algebras over its base by the strict-henselization triples construction, and both targets are henselian local with residue field $K$. In the application over R the source is C, already ind-etale over R, and the target D is made an R-algebra by R to S to A to D. No ind-etale presentation of D over R is required.

source.place: Lemma Tag 08HR (lemma-map-into-henselian-colimit) applied over A and over R

proof.text: The composite $f\circ g$ is an $R$-algebra endomorphism of $C$ with preimage $m_C$ equal to $m_C$ and residue map the identity of $K$, so the uniqueness clause of lem-weil-pbc-map-into-henselian-colimit over $R$ gives $f\circ g=\operatorname{id}_C$. The maps $A\to C\to D$ and $A\to D$ agree: they agree on $S$ by Step 2 and the uniqueness clause for the single etale $R$-algebra $S$, and $A=S_q$ is generated from $S$ by inverting elements outside $q$. Therefore $g\circ f$ is an $A$-algebra endomorphism of $D$ with the same local and residue properties, and uniqueness over $A$ gives $g\circ f=\operatorname{id}_D$. The construction of $f$ also gives compatibility $S\to A\to D\to C=S\to C$.

source.place: Lemma Tag 08HR, uniqueness clause, applied first over R and then over A

proof.text: For any other ring equivalence with the stated S-compatibility, localization gives agreement of the induced maps on A. Equality of the residue maps and the uniqueness clause of the henselian-colimit mapping theorem over A then identify the equivalences.

proof_origin.place: Lemma Tag 04GW and Lemma Tag 04GP, with Lemma Tag 08HR for the comparison maps

theorem strictHenselization_comparison
    (R : CommRingCat.{u}) [IsLocalRing R]
    (K : Type u) [Field K]
    [Algebra ((Spec R).residueField (IsLocalRing.closedPoint R)) K]
    [IsSepClosure ((Spec R).residueField (IsLocalRing.closedPoint R)) K]
    (c : Cocone (etaleResidueTriplesRingDiagram R (IsLocalRing.closedPoint R) K
      (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap
        ((Spec R).residueField (IsLocalRing.closedPoint R)) K))))
    (hc : IsColimit c)
    (ρ : R ⟶ c.pt) (ψ : c.pt →+* K)
    (hρ : ∀ s, s.α ≫ c.ι.app s = ρ)
    (hψ : ∀ s, ψ.comp (c.ι.app s).hom =
      ((ΓSpecIso s.B).inv ≫ (Spec s.B).Γevaluation s.q ≫ s.φ).hom)
    (t : EtaleResidueTriples R (IsLocalRing.closedPoint R) K
      (CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap
        ((Spec R).residueField (IsLocalRing.closedPoint R)) K)))
    (A : CommRingCat.{u}) [Algebra t.B A] [IsLocalization.AtPrime A t.q.asIdeal]
    [IsLocalRing A]
    (χA : (Spec A).residueField (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A) ⟶ CommRingCat.of K)
    (hχA : CommRingCat.ofHom (algebraMap t.B A) ≫ (ΓSpecIso A).inv ≫
      (Spec A).Γevaluation (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A) ≫ χA =
      (ΓSpecIso t.B).inv ≫ (Spec t.B).Γevaluation t.q ≫ t.φ)
    (d : Cocone (etaleResidueTriplesRingDiagram A (IsLocalRing.closedPoint A) K χA))
    (hd : IsColimit d) (δ : A ⟶ d.pt) (ψD : d.pt →+* K)
    (hδ : ∀ s, s.α ≫ d.ι.app s = δ)
    (hψD : ∀ s, ψD.comp (d.ι.app s).hom =
      ((ΓSpecIso s.B).inv ≫ (Spec s.B).Γevaluation s.q ≫ s.φ).hom) :
    ∃! e : d.pt ≃+* c.pt,
      e.toRingHom.comp (δ.hom.comp (algebraMap t.B A)) = (c.ι.app t).hom ∧
      ψ.comp e.toRingHom = ψD
